findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of mold on the baffles of the ice machine. Discussed with PIC and machine was cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently and free of mold build up. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C) (Pf) The facility did not have employee reporting agreements available during the inspection. These agreements are needed in order to ensure employees do not report to work while sick, which could spread illness or disease. Employees in the facility signed reporting agreements during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths were wet and laying on the bar counter top. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Cloths sitting out were moved to sanitizer solution. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed all the soda nozzle holders to be soiled with mildew. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation. The soda nozzle holders were cleaned during the inspection, and the manager stated new ones have already been ordered. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07. Allergen awareness training.
(b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed PIC wash hands at 3 compartment sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Rewash hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.15 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste. (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed 2 soiled soda nozzles at the bar. Observed soil build up in the ice machine.  CORRECTED- Food contact surfaces were washed rinsed and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.comment: Observed wet wiping cloth stored on dirty side of 3 compartment sink drainboard. Store wet wiping cloths submerged in sanitizer solution.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14 (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. (C)

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed knife on prep line stored between in the gap between the counter and hot-holding equipment. Observed knives stored in wooden knife block. Store knives on clean, sanitized surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12 Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
No CFM has completed allergen awareness training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed baffle of ice machine to be soiled with black slime mold. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed  Date of 2/27 marked on green peppers and fish sauce in cooler exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41?F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text: 4-101.11  (P) Observed  In-use cutting board with deep gouges and grooves. The cutting board can no longer be washed and sanitized properly to prevent pathogen growth. Reference 4-101.11.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C)Floor in the kitchen area behind fryer was found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed multiple PHFs in the walk-in cooler that were at 49F or higher. All PHFs in this cooler were voluntarily discarded during the inpsection. Ensure that the temperatures of these cooling units are regularly monitored (see violation 4).
750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in cooler to not be operating correctly. Staff state it has been a continuous issue. The owner will contact AirMasters for repairs. The unit was found to be running around 48F after the door being closed for 20 minutes. The unit quickly rose in air temperature and almost all the PHFs within the cooler were out of temperature. Raw beef was saved due to the fact that it had been placed into the cooler to thaw and was found at 40F. Raw beef moved to another walk-in unit. Discussed follow-up with owner and a tenative follow-up for 05/25/2018, if the cooler has been repaired. 
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the ice scoop at the bar to be stored with the handle in the ice. Ice scoops shall be stored in one of the manners listed below. Ice scoop properly placed in ice. 
750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed utensils that would be utilized for food tomorrow to be being stored in a dirty state. Ensure that all utensils and equipment are properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the end of use to prevent a potential for cross contamination, as well as a pest issue. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed soiled linen being stored over the stove top in the kitchen on the soiled utensils from violation 22. Ensure that soiled linens are stored in a proper manner to prevent a pest issue/cross-contamination issue in the future. Linen moved during the inspection. 
750-1380b Soiled clothes and linens shall be stored in non-absorbent containers or washable laundry bags until removed for laundering. Properly store soiled linens.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed chicken in the walk in cooler in the kitchen to be cooling without the time that the cooling process began to be indicated. Chicken had reported to have been cooling for approximately 1 hour and was probed at an internal temperature of 140F. Chicken was taken from the cooler and placed on an ice bath. Foods must cool to 70F within 2 hours and to 41F or below within an additional 4 hours.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed pork in a the crock pot to be probed at an internal temperature of 106F. This had previously been cooked and was being reheated. It was reported that this had been reheated on the stove before being transferred to the crock pot, but it was unknown to what temperature it was reheated. Reheat all foods to 165F before being hot held at 135F or above, or alternatively, reheat to order. Pork was to be pulled and put back on the stove for reheating.
750-210  Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165°F or higher through out the product. Properly reheat food to 165°F or above.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on the lid to the prep cooler. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer solution in between use.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the inside surfaces of the microwave with food splash, 2) the ice flap in the ice machine with black mold, 3) oven handle there the tongs are handing, 4) soda nozzles at the bar with syrup accumulation. Wash, rinse and sanitize these food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
The hand sink in the kitchen is slow draining. Repair plumbing so sink drains properly.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
No certified FSSMC present at the time of the inspection. Ryan thought that he had one, but his certificate ended up being expired. Facility is required to have at least one certified FSSMC present at all times potentially hazardous foods are being prepared or served. Owner has requested information on classes, which will be sent out.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
1) Observed chicken in the walk in cooler inside cooling since 8:30 this morning that was not marked with the time the cooling process began. Cooling as an active process was discussed. Cool to 70F within 2 hours and 41F or below within an additional 4 hours. 2) Observed a container of spices on the shelf above the crock pots to not be labeled. Label all items removed from their original container.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed pork in the walk in cooler outside to not be date marked with the date of preparation. It was reported that this was probably made yesterday and should be date marked as such. The majority of items are prepared on a daily basis, however, any of the items that are open, ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods must be marked with the date of opening or preparation and held no longer than 7 days maximum.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: No thermometer was observed in the walk in coolers. The built in thermometers on the units either are not working or were not accurate during the inspection. Provide thermometers in each of these walk in coolers.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Employee did not wash his hands before putting on gloves to begin serving food. Hand washing was discussed. Even if employees wash hands in the restroom, they MUST wash hands again in the kitchen before returning to food prep.
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the ice scoop to be stored in a soiled container on top of the ice machine. These were taken to dish during the inspection. Store scoop clean and dry. 2) Observed the in use crock pots in the kitchen to have old food stuck on the sides of the insert and the lids to be soiled. Crock pot inserts should be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use. If cooling the food within from one day to the next, it should be transferred to a clean container so the inserts may be washed. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:

Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible

CORRECTED> Hand sink was blocked with a bus tub at the beginning of the inspection and the roll of paper towels was underneath this tub in the sink and they were dry. Bus tub was moved during the inspection.
750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed the light in the walk in cooler outside to not be shielded. Provide a light shield for this light or a shatterproof bulb.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed beef and beans in the walk in cooler inside to be probed at an internal temperature of 56F. This was reported to have been placed in the walk in around 8:30 this morning so it has now been approximately 5.5 hours and it is unknown whether this product reached 70F or below by 10:30. Item was discarded. Also observed cheese sauce cooling in the walk in cooler outside that was probed at an internal temperature of 89F and was reported to have been i there since 9 AM. This cheese sauce was discarded. Another cheese sauce was probed at 63F and was placed in an ice bath to rapidly cool to 41F or below. 2) Observed orange juice sitting on top of the keg in the keg cooler to be probed at 48F. Items in the bottom of this cooler were 39F. Cease storing juice and things requiring refrigeration on top of the kegs. OJ was discarded.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.comment: The single use utensils are being stored in a grey caddy with the eating surfaces exposed to the air and passers by. 750-880 Single-service knives, forks and spoons packaged in bulk shall be inserted into holders to protect these items from contamination and present the handle of the utensils to the consumer unless the utensils are pre-wrapped or pre-packaged. Store utensils properly protected.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Floor in the men's rest room has a broken tile in the corner next to the urinal that is broken. 750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.comment: Clean utensils are stored in a bucket with some crumbs in the bottom. 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.   Clean bucket and utensils and maintain bucket free of crumbs.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: The keg cooler holding juices and mixers does not have a thermometer upon arrival. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F. A Thermometer was placed in the cooler.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Wet cloths used for wiping are observed to be stored on the bar top. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Store wet wiping cloths properly.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Keg cooler behind bar has water accumulated in the bottom.750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean cooler/remove water. Water in the cooler can be a sign that the cooler will malfunction. Watch cooler air temperature using thermometer that was added to the cooler.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed improper cooling of the following foods: ground beef, cheese sauce, and shredded chicken. Items were not properly marked with time removed from heat control. Mark items that are being cooled with time removed from heat control. Facility has two hours reduce temperature from 135F or above to 70F, and then an additional four hours to have food temperatures reduced to 41F or below. Items were placed in an ice bath to speed up cooling.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed all the ice bins throughout establishment to be missing covers. Provide covers for ice bins that are used for human consumption.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ice deflector in the ice machine to be soiled with an accumulation of mold. Remove ice and wash, rinse, and sanitize inside ice machine.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the general surfaces of the grill, oven, and burner to be soiled with an accumulation of grease and char. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.comment:
